signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.15, testing the 200-hour moving average as geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz escalate. While the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains the primary structural support, Pentagon headlines regarding military force in Iran introduce acute intervention and haven-linked volatility. The options market signals significant downside concern, with 25d risk reversals at -1.96 showing a strong put skew that contrasts with neutral speculative positioning (JPY COT pctl 38). This negative VRP of -1.6% suggests implied volatility sits below realized levels, marking a period of unusual complacency before this latest geopolitical shock. A sustained break above 160.00 remains the key threshold for BoJ verbal or physical intervention. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage persists while geopolitical headlines cap immediate upside momentum. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 66% hike priced) 18 Sep — hike bias intact. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a broader carry unwind and haven-led JPY bid.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF emerges as the dominant G10 trend this week as AUD outperforms the peer group by 0.613% while CHF lags as the weakest performer. This divergence is fundamentally supported by a massive +435bp carry advantage in favor of the AUD, with the RBA on hold at 4.35% versus the SNB at 0.00%. The technical backdrop reinforces this move, as AUD/USD remains positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6954-0.7057), while USD/CHF holds below its 20/50 day moving averages. Despite the strong performance, retail sentiment shows an 87% extreme short on AUD/CHF, providing a contrarian propellant for further upside if these positions are forced to cover. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry-driven outperformance remains the primary G10 theme. Catalyst: SEK rate decision 25 Aug for secondary G10 vol. Risk: Risk-off sentiment pushes VIX toward 25, compressing the AUD/CHF carry trade.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Extreme + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3631, supported by a COT LF net long of +46,070 which sits at the 94th percentile of its 52-week range. This crowded positioning is accompanied by a significant volatility risk premium, with GBP/USD IV at 11.0% vs HV30 at 5.9%, creating a +5.1% VRP. The options market is pricing in elevated protection demand, potentially reflecting caution as price holds well above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3395-1.3485). While the SONIA-SOFR spread is nearly neutral at -10bp, the persistent data misses in the US (ESI -15.0) have allowed Sterling to maintain its momentum despite the heavy speculative weight. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; momentum leader status intact until positioning reaches total exhaustion. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: A sharp 4W positioning reversal in COT data signaling a top in the current cycle.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Trade Tension + ESI Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD holds at 1.3846 following high-impact headlines regarding Trump's trade threats toward Canada. This geopolitical tension offsets a strong positive CAD Economic Surprise Index of +22.9, which suggests Canadian domestic data remains resilient compared to persistent US misses. Technically, USD/CAD is positioned below its SMA20, 50, and 200 levels (1.3843-1.4061), suggesting the long-term trend remains under pressure despite the immediate trade-related bounce. Speculative positioning remains heavily net short CAD (lev_net -89,836, pctl 13), leaving the pair vulnerable to a squeeze if trade rhetoric softens. Trade bias: Neutral USD/CAD; trade headline risks balance out the positive Canadian macro data. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Further trade escalation from the US triggers a move back toward the 1.4000 handle.
